name: NCP718ASN330T1G
title: 300 mA low-dropout regulator, 2.5 V to 24 V input, low quiescent current
summary: The NCP718 is a 300 mA linear regulator that runs from 2.5 V up to 24 V while drawing about 4 µA with no load. Fixed outputs from 1.2 V to 5 V hold within ±2 % (±3 % below 1.8 V) across line, load and temperature, and an adjustable version sets 1.2 V to 5 V with two resistors. It is stable with 1 µF ceramic capacitors, starts softly, and has current limit, an input-to-output voltage dependent SOA limit and thermal shutdown. A versions add an output discharge switch; B versions omit it. Packages are TSOT-23-5 and a 2 mm × 2 mm WDFN6.

circuits.title: Typical application schematic, fixed versions
circuits.description: A fixed-output NCP718 with one 1 µF ceramic capacitor from IN to ground and another from OUT to ground. EN is the on/off control: high runs the regulator, low shuts it down. The NC/ADJ pin has no connection on a fixed version.

circuits.title: Adjustable version connection schematic
circuits.description: The adjustable NCP718 with 1 µF ceramic capacitors at IN and OUT. R2 runs from the output to the ADJ pin and R1 from ADJ to ground; the loop holds ADJ at 1.2 V, so VOUT = 1.2 V × (1 + R2/R1), settable from 1.2 V to 5 V. EN switches the regulator on and off.

operation.text: Fixed outputs are offered from 1.2 V to 5 V (other fixed values on request) and an adjustable version covers 1.2 V to 5 V. A-suffix parts (NCP718A) have an active output discharge; B-suffix parts (NCP718B) do not. MT in the part number is WDFN6, SN is TSOT-23-5.
EN above 1.2 V switches the regulator on; below 0.4 V it shuts down and the input draws 0.1 µA typical. EN draws about 100 nA at 5.5 V. EN may go up to VIN + 0.3 V.
An internal soft start ramps the output at turn-on, limiting inrush current and overshoot.
On A versions a switch from OUT to GND, about 100 Ω, turns on when EN is low and empties the output capacitor.

The output current limit lies between 300 mA and 800 mA at VIN = VOUT + 1 V, and the output may be shorted indefinitely. A safe-operating-area limit lowers the allowed current as VIN − VOUT rises, for both steady and pulsed loads.
The regulator turns off at a junction temperature of about 165 °C and restarts after it cools by about 25 °C. For reliable operation the junction is kept at or below 125 °C.

At least 1 µF of X5R or X7R ceramic between IN and GND. It shunts noise riding on the supply and masks the inductance and resistance of the input wiring during load steps. More capacitance and lower ESR give better line transient response.
The regulator is stable with ceramic capacitors of 1 µF or more and needs no minimum ESR. X5R and X7R dielectrics are preferred for their small change with temperature.

How much power the part can shed depends on the board: pad layout, board material and ambient temperature. Junction-to-air resistance is 65 °C/W in WDFN6 and 235 °C/W in TSOT-23-5. The NC pins may be grounded to help with heat.

Wide VIN and GND traces: a high-impedance supply or ground path picks up noise and can make the regulator misbehave. Put the external parts, the output capacitor first, right at the chip with short traces.
R1 below 100 kΩ and R2 below 1 MΩ keep the change of ADJ pin current over temperature (0.1 µA typical, 1.0 µA maximum) from shifting the output.
Operating the output at about 5.2 V can damage the part. The output pin is rated to 6 V at most.
